question.text: What must a first-time applicant for a license, permit or ID card bring?

answer.text: A first-time applicant for a license, learner's permit or ID card must bring originals or verifiable certified copies proving identity, lawful status in the US and full Social Security number, plus two documents proving Indiana residency.

teaching.text: First-time applicants bring originals or certified copies for four things: identity, lawful status, full Social Security number and two Indiana address proofs. Remember: identity, status, number, two addresses.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A first-time applicant for a license, learner's permit or ID card must bring originals or verifiable certified copies proving identity, lawful status in the US and full Social Security number, plus two documents proving Indiana residency.

question.text: What should someone renewing or replacing an Indiana credential bring to get a Real ID?

answer.text: Someone renewing, amending or replacing a current Indiana credential should bring original or certified documents to a branch if they want a Real ID-compliant credential.

teaching.text: Renewing, amending or replacing a card? Bring original or certified documents to a branch if you want it Real ID-compliant. Remember: originals for a Real ID.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Someone renewing, amending or replacing a current Indiana credential should bring original or certified documents to a branch if they want a Real ID-compliant credential.

question.text: What kind of US birth certificate proves identity, and which kind is refused?

answer.text: A US birth certificate used as identity proof must be an original or certified copy issued by a government agency, and unofficial hospital birth certificates are not accepted.

teaching.text: Only a government-issued original or certified birth certificate counts; the souvenir kind from a hospital is refused. Remember: certified, never hospital souvenirs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A US birth certificate used as identity proof must be an original or certified copy issued by a government agency, and unofficial hospital birth certificates are not accepted.

question.text: When can a US passport or passport card prove identity?

answer.text: A US passport or passport card can prove identity only if it is not expired.

teaching.text: A US passport or passport card works for identity only while it is unexpired. Remember: unexpired passports only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A US passport or passport card can prove identity only if it is not expired.

question.text: When does a foreign passport prove identity?

answer.text: A foreign passport proves identity only when it is unexpired and carries a US visa with an approved I-ninety-four form showing the most recent admission or current status.

teaching.text: A foreign passport must be unexpired and carry a US visa with an approved arrival record form to prove identity. Remember: unexpired, with visa and arrival record.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A foreign passport proves identity only when it is unexpired and carries a US visa with an approved I-ninety-four form showing the most recent admission or current status.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: unexpired, with visa and arrival record

question.text: When can a Permanent Resident Card or Employment Authorization Card prove identity?

answer.text: A Permanent Resident Card or Employment Authorization Card can prove identity only if it is unexpired and its lawful status has been verified.

teaching.text: Permanent Resident and Employment Authorization Cards must be unexpired and have verified lawful status. Remember: unexpired and verified.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Permanent Resident Card or Employment Authorization Card can prove identity only if it is unexpired and its lawful status has been verified.

question.text: What can a delayed birth certificate prove for someone born outside the US?

answer.text: A person born outside the US may use a delayed birth certificate to prove identity, but not lawful status.

teaching.text: A delayed birth certificate can prove who you are, but not your lawful status. Remember: identity yes, status no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A person born outside the US may use a delayed birth certificate to prove identity, but not lawful status.

question.text: Can a delayed birth certificate prove lawful status?

answer.text: A delayed birth certificate for someone born abroad works for identity, while lawful status must be shown another way.

teaching.text: After using a delayed birth certificate for identity, bring a separate document for lawful status. Remember: status needs another document.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A delayed birth certificate for someone born abroad works for identity, while lawful status must be shown another way.

question.text: What must be true of an amended birth certificate showing a new name or birth date?

answer.text: An amended birth certificate showing a new legal name or date of birth must be certified and filed with the vital statistics office in the state of birth.

teaching.text: An amended birth certificate showing a new name or birth date must be certified and filed with your birth state's vital statistics office. Remember: certified and filed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An amended birth certificate showing a new legal name or date of birth must be certified and filed with the vital statistics office in the state of birth.

question.text: What can a non-citizen use as identity proof after getting a Real ID credential?

answer.text: A non-citizen who received a Real ID-compliant credential using one of the listed documents may use that credential as identity proof in later transactions.

teaching.text: A non-citizen who earned a Real ID card with a listed document can use that card as identity proof next time. Remember: Real ID card proves later.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A non-citizen who received a Real ID-compliant credential using one of the listed documents may use that credential as identity proof in later transactions.

question.text: What must you show if your legal name or date of birth differs from your identity documents?

answer.text: If your legal name or date of birth differs from your identity documents, you must show legal proof of the change, such as a marriage license, divorce decree or court order.

teaching.text: If your name or birth date has changed, bring the legal proof, such as a marriage license, divorce decree or court order. Remember: prove every change.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If your legal name or date of birth differs from your identity documents, you must show legal proof of the change, such as a marriage license, divorce decree or court order.

question.text: For a US citizen, what proves lawful status?

answer.text: For a US citizen, the document used to prove identity also proves lawful status.

teaching.text: For US citizens, the identity document does double duty and proves lawful status too. Remember: citizen identity covers status.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a US citizen, the document used to prove identity also proves lawful status.

question.text: When does a Notice of Action count as lawful status proof?

answer.text: A Notice of Action form proves lawful status only if the BMV verifies that DHS received it without denying action and the applicant also submits pertaining federal-agency documents showing lawful status.

teaching.text: A Notice of Action counts for lawful status once the BMV confirms DHS received it and has not denied it. Remember: verified plus pertaining federal docs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Notice of Action form proves lawful status only if the BMV verifies that DHS received it without denying action and the applicant also submits pertaining federal-agency documents showing lawful status.

question.text: Is proof of an asylum application a lawful status document?

answer.text: Proof of an asylum application verified by DHS is listed as a lawful status document.

teaching.text: A DHS-verified asylum application is on the list of lawful status documents. Remember: verified asylum proof counts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Proof of an asylum application verified by DHS is listed as a lawful status document.

question.text: Which documents can prove your Social Security number?

answer.text: A Social Security number can be proven with a document showing your name and full number, such as a Social Security card, a W-two, a one thousand ninety-nine or a pre-printed pay stub.

teaching.text: Prove your Social Security number with a document showing your name and full number, such as the card, a W-two, a ten-ninety-nine or a pre-printed pay stub. Remember: card, W-two, pay stub.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Social Security number can be proven with a document showing your name and full number, such as a Social Security card, a W-two, a one thousand ninety-nine or a pre-printed pay stub.

question.text: What does an applicant who does not qualify for a Social Security number submit?

answer.text: An applicant not authorized to work in the US who does not qualify for a Social Security number must submit documents showing that, and may be asked for a valid I-ninety-four instead.

teaching.text: If you do not qualify for a number and cannot work in the US, bring documents showing that, and you may be asked for an arrival record form instead. Remember: proof of no number.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An applicant not authorized to work in the US who does not qualify for a Social Security number must submit documents showing that, and may be asked for a valid I-ninety-four instead.

question.text: Who may list a post office box as a residential address?

answer.text: Only applicants in the Indiana Attorney General's Address Confidentiality Program may list a post office box as their residential address.

teaching.text: A post office box is not a home address, except for people in the Attorney General's Address Confidentiality Program. Remember: PO box only if confidential.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Only applicants in the Indiana Attorney General's Address Confidentiality Program may list a post office box as their residential address.

question.text: Which bills and statements prove residency, and how recent must they be?

answer.text: A utility, credit card, doctor or hospital bill, a bank statement or a pre-printed pay stub can prove residency if it shows your name and residential address and is dated within sixty days of applying.

teaching.text: Bills, bank statements and pay stubs prove residency only if they show your name and home address and are no more than sixty days old. Remember: sixty days for bills.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A utility, credit card, doctor or hospital bill, a bank statement or a pre-printed pay stub can prove residency if it shows your name and residential address and is dated within sixty days of applying.

question.text: How recent must an insurance policy be to prove residency?

answer.text: A homeowner's, renter's or vehicle insurance policy proves residency if it shows your name and residential address and is dated within one year of applying.

teaching.text: An insurance policy for your home, rental or vehicle can be up to one year old and still prove residency. Remember: insurance within a year.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A homeowner's, renter's or vehicle insurance policy proves residency if it shows your name and residential address and is dated within one year of applying.

question.text: How do the date windows for a W-two or tax bill and an insurance policy differ?

answer.text: A W-two, property or excise tax bill, or benefits statement must be dated in the current or prior year, whereas an insurance policy must be dated within one year of the application.

teaching.text: Tax forms and benefit statements must be from this year or last, while insurance policies may be up to a year old. Remember: this year, last year, or one.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A W-two, property or excise tax bill, or benefits statement must be dated in the current or prior year, whereas an insurance policy must be dated within one year of the application.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: this year, last year, or one

question.text: Which voter and school documents are accepted residency proof?

answer.text: An Indiana voter registration card and public or private school records showing an enrolled student's name and residential address are among the accepted residency documents.

teaching.text: An Indiana voter card, or school records showing a student's name and home address, also prove residency. Remember: voter card, school records.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An Indiana voter registration card and public or private school records showing an enrolled student's name and residential address are among the accepted residency documents.

question.text: Can a postal change of address confirmation prove residency?

answer.text: A US Postal Service change of address confirmation showing both prior and current address can prove residency.

teaching.text: A postal change of address confirmation showing your old and new address can prove residency. Remember: old and new address shown.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A US Postal Service change of address confirmation showing both prior and current address can prove residency.

question.text: Who may file an Indiana Residency Affidavit?

answer.text: An applicant without two residency documents may file an Indiana Residency Affidavit if they are incapacitated, homeless, living with a relative or friend, or living in a motor vehicle.

teaching.text: Short on residency documents? An affidavit is possible if you are incapacitated, homeless, living with someone or living in a vehicle. Remember: affidavit when papers fall short.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An applicant without two residency documents may file an Indiana Residency Affidavit if they are incapacitated, homeless, living with a relative or friend, or living in a motor vehicle.

question.text: What must a relative or friend do to sign an affidavit for someone living with them?

answer.text: For an applicant living with a relative or friend, that person, aged at least eighteen, signs the affidavit at a branch and shows their own Indiana credential, identity proof and two Indiana address documents.

teaching.text: When you live with a relative or friend, they sign the affidavit at a branch and bring their own credential, identity proof and two address documents. Remember: host signs, shows proof.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For an applicant living with a relative or friend, that person, aged at least eighteen, signs the affidavit at a branch and shows their own Indiana credential, identity proof and two Indiana address documents.

question.text: Who signs the affidavit for an incapacitated applicant, and for a homeless applicant?

answer.text: For an incapacitated applicant the affidavit is signed by a resident guardian or caregiver aged at least eighteen, while for a homeless applicant it is signed by a representative of the agency or nonprofit that serves them.

teaching.text: Caregivers sign for incapacitated applicants, and an agency or nonprofit representative signs for homeless applicants. Remember: caregiver or agency signs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For an incapacitated applicant the affidavit is signed by a resident guardian or caregiver aged at least eighteen, while for a homeless applicant it is signed by a representative of the agency or nonprofit that serves them.

question.text: What does an applicant living in a motor vehicle need for the affidavit?

answer.text: An applicant living in a motor vehicle such as a motor home needs another Indiana resident to sign the affidavit at a branch and must show Indiana income tax payment plus current title and registration records with the BMV.

teaching.text: Living in a motor home or other vehicle means another Indiana resident signs, and you show Indiana tax payment plus title and registration. Remember: resident signer, taxes, title.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An applicant living in a motor vehicle such as a motor home needs another Indiana resident to sign the affidavit at a branch and must show Indiana income tax payment plus current title and registration records with the BMV.

question.text: Which documents does the BMV accept, and which may it refuse?

answer.text: The BMV accepts only original documents or certified copies from the issuing agency and may refuse any document that looks fraudulent, unreliable, altered or expired.

teaching.text: The BMV wants originals or certified copies from the issuing agency and may turn down anything that looks fake, altered or expired. Remember: originals or certified copies.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The BMV accepts only original documents or certified copies from the issuing agency and may refuse any document that looks fraudulent, unreliable, altered or expired.

question.text: What language must documents be in, and what must match Social Security records?

answer.text: All documents must be in English or come with a verifiably accurate English translation, and your legal name and date of birth must match Social Security Administration records.

teaching.text: Documents must be in English or come with an accurate translation, and your name and birth date must match Social Security records. Remember: English, matching names.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: All documents must be in English or come with a verifiably accurate English translation, and your legal name and date of birth must match Social Security Administration records.

question.text: What must a document translation include?

answer.text: A translation must be typed on the letterhead of a government entity, accredited school or translation agency, with a signed statement of accuracy and competence, and not done for a family member, friend or business associate.

teaching.text: Translations must be typed on government, accredited school or agency letterhead with a signed statement, and never done for family, friends or associates. Remember: letterhead, signed, not family.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A translation must be typed on the letterhead of a government entity, accredited school or translation agency, with a signed statement of accuracy and competence, and not done for a family member, friend or business associate.

question.text: What must a translator's statement say?

answer.text: A translator's statement must attest that the translation is accurate and that the translator is competent.

teaching.text: The translator signs a statement that the translation is accurate and that they are competent. Remember: accurate and competent.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A translator's statement must attest that the translation is accurate and that the translator is competent.

question.text: What credential may a US citizen with a valid non-compliant card choose, and how is it marked?

answer.text: A US citizen holding a valid non-compliant Indiana credential may choose another non-compliant credential, which is printed with NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES on the front.

teaching.text: Citizens with a valid non-compliant card may choose another non-compliant card, marked NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES. Remember: not for Real ID.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A US citizen holding a valid non-compliant Indiana credential may choose another non-compliant credential, which is printed with NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES on the front.

question.text: What is the leading contributor to teen crashes?

answer.text: The leading contributor to teen crashes is errant, risky or distracted driving.

teaching.text: Most teen crashes come down to errant, risky or distracted driving. Remember: risky, distracted teens crash.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The leading contributor to teen crashes is errant, risky or distracted driving.

question.text: How does each passenger affect a teen driver's crash chance?

answer.text: The manual says the chance of a crash doubles with each passenger in a teen driver's vehicle.

teaching.text: Every extra passenger in a teen's car doubles the crash chance, according to the manual. Remember: each passenger doubles risk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The manual says the chance of a crash doubles with each passenger in a teen driver's vehicle.

question.text: Where do most multi-vehicle crashes involving teens happen?

answer.text: Most multi-vehicle crashes involving teens happen at intersections.

teaching.text: Teens are most likely to crash with other vehicles at intersections. Remember: intersections catch teens.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Most multi-vehicle crashes involving teens happen at intersections.

question.text: Which factor is common in single-vehicle crashes, and which in multiple-vehicle crashes?

answer.text: Illegal or unsafe speed is a common factor in single-vehicle crashes, while driver inattention is a common factor in multiple-vehicle crashes.

teaching.text: Speed is the common thread in single-car crashes, and inattention in multi-car crashes. Remember: speed alone, inattention together.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Illegal or unsafe speed is a common factor in single-vehicle crashes, while driver inattention is a common factor in multiple-vehicle crashes.

question.text: How do impaired teen drivers affect serious injuries and deaths in teen crashes?

answer.text: Teen drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs are a small share but account for a much higher share of serious injuries and deaths in teen crashes.

teaching.text: Impaired teens are few, yet they account for a much larger share of serious injuries and deaths. Remember: few impaired, many harmed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Teen drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs are a small share but account for a much higher share of serious injuries and deaths in teen crashes.

question.text: When should you not enter an intersection on a yellow light?

answer.text: Unless you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should not enter after it turns yellow.

teaching.text: Already in the intersection when it turns yellow? Keep going. Not yet in? Do not enter. Remember: yellow means do not enter.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Unless you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should not enter after it turns yellow.

question.text: What should you be ready to do even on a green light?

answer.text: Even with a green light, be ready to stop as you approach an intersection in case the light changes.

teaching.text: Even on green, approach intersections ready to stop if the light changes. Remember: ready to stop on green.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Even with a green light, be ready to stop as you approach an intersection in case the light changes.

question.text: What does the manual say about phones and some over-the-counter drugs?

answer.text: Talking on the phone or texting while driving is against the law, and even some over-the-counter drugs can cause drowsiness.

teaching.text: Phone calls and texting while driving are against the law, and some over-the-counter medicines can make you drowsy. Remember: no phones, watch medicines.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Talking on the phone or texting while driving is against the law, and even some over-the-counter drugs can cause drowsiness.

question.text: What habits are teens advised to follow with seats, mirrors, radio and music?

answer.text: Teens are advised to adjust seats and mirrors before each drive, wait until stopped to adjust the radio, and avoid loud music that could hide a siren or horn.

teaching.text: Set your seat and mirrors before you drive, adjust the radio only when stopped, and keep music low enough to hear sirens and horns. Remember: set up before you go.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Teens are advised to adjust seats and mirrors before each drive, wait until stopped to adjust the radio, and avoid loud music that could hide a siren or horn.

question.text: What does the manual say about seat belts for teens?

answer.text: A seat belt is required by law and is the most effective way to lower the risk of being hurt or killed in a crash.

teaching.text: Seat belts are the law and the most effective way to lower the risk of injury or death in a crash. Remember: belts required, best protection.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A seat belt is required by law and is the most effective way to lower the risk of being hurt or killed in a crash.

question.text: When and in what conditions should parents practice driving with their teen?

answer.text: Parents are advised to practice driving with their teen during the learner's permit period and the first year of licensed driving, in varied conditions such as wet roads, snow, highways and night driving.

teaching.text: Parents should practice with teens through the permit period and the first licensed year, on wet roads, in snow, on highways and at night. Remember: practice in all conditions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parents are advised to practice driving with their teen during the learner's permit period and the first year of licensed driving, in varied conditions such as wet roads, snow, highways and night driving.

question.text: What are parents urged to do for their teen driver?

answer.text: Parents are urged to set a good example, require seat belts, choose vehicles for safety rather than image, and grant progressive privileges as the teen shows good judgment.

teaching.text: Parents lead by example, require belts, pick safe vehicles over flashy ones, and add privileges as the teen earns them. Remember: model, require, choose safety.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parents are urged to set a good example, require seat belts, choose vehicles for safety rather than image, and grant progressive privileges as the teen shows good judgment.

question.text: How does the manual describe driver education and the parents' role?

answer.text: The manual calls driver education a first step and says parents play a crucial role in teaching teens to drive.

teaching.text: Driver education is only a first step, and parents play a crucial role in teaching teens to drive. Remember: parents finish the lesson.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The manual calls driver education a first step and says parents play a crucial role in teaching teens to drive.

question.text: What must anyone under eighteen wear on an off-road vehicle?

answer.text: Anyone under eighteen operating or riding an off-road vehicle must wear a helmet meeting US Department of Transportation standards, and an owner may not knowingly let someone under eighteen ride without one.

teaching.text: Anyone under eighteen on an off-road vehicle needs a helmet meeting US Department of Transportation standards, and owners may not knowingly allow riding without one. Remember: helmets under eighteen.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Anyone under eighteen operating or riding an off-road vehicle must wear a helmet meeting US Department of Transportation standards, and an owner may not knowingly let someone under eighteen ride without one.

question.text: Where can an eligible person apply to register to vote during a credential transaction?

answer.text: Anyone eligible to vote may apply to register while completing a credential transaction at a branch, on myBMV.com or at a BMV Connect kiosk.

teaching.text: You can apply to register to vote during a credential transaction at a branch, online or at a kiosk. Remember: register to vote here.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Anyone eligible to vote may apply to register while completing a credential transaction at a branch, on myBMV.com or at a BMV Connect kiosk.

question.text: What does the BMV do for a male under twenty-six who authorizes Selective Service registration?

answer.text: When authorized by a male under twenty-six getting a new or renewed license, the BMV sends his information to register him with the Selective Service, and failing to register is a felony.

teaching.text: With his permission, the BMV registers a male under twenty-six with the Selective Service when he gets or renews a license, and failing to register is a felony. Remember: license links to Selective Service.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When authorized by a male under twenty-six getting a new or renewed license, the BMV sends his information to register him with the Selective Service, and failing to register is a felony.

question.text: What penalties can failing to register with the Selective Service bring?

answer.text: Failing to register with the Selective Service can bring up to five years in prison and a two hundred fifty thousand dollars fine, and registration applies to US citizens.

teaching.text: Not registering with the Selective Service can mean up to five years in prison and a large fine, and registration applies to US citizens. Remember: skipping registration is serious.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Failing to register with the Selective Service can bring up to five years in prison and a two hundred fifty thousand dollars fine, and registration applies to US citizens.

question.text: Where are BMV forms available, and what about people not at a branch who want to register to vote?

answer.text: BMV forms are available on IN.gov slash BMV or at any branch, and mail-in voter registration forms exist for people not at a branch.

teaching.text: BMV forms are online or at any branch, and mail-in voter registration forms exist for people not at a branch. Remember: forms online or branch.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: BMV forms are available on IN.gov slash BMV or at any branch, and mail-in voter registration forms exist for people not at a branch.

question.text: How can vehicle registration be renewed, and how long do plates and stickers take?

answer.text: Vehicle registration can be renewed by phone, by mail, online at myBMV.com or at a BMV Connect kiosk, and for online, phone and mail renewals the plates and stickers arrive in about twenty-one days.

teaching.text: Renew vehicle registration by phone, mail, online or at a kiosk, and expect plates and stickers in about twenty-one days for online, phone and mail renewals. Remember: phone, mail, online, kiosk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicle registration can be renewed by phone, by mail, online at myBMV.com or at a BMV Connect kiosk, and for online, phone and mail renewals the plates and stickers arrive in about twenty-one days.

question.text: How should checks for registration renewal be made out?

answer.text: Checks for registration renewal should be made out to BMV or Bureau of Motor Vehicles.

teaching.text: Make registration renewal checks out to BMV or Bureau of Motor Vehicles. Remember: checks to the BMV.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Checks for registration renewal should be made out to BMV or Bureau of Motor Vehicles.
